extraction.name: RoboFAC
extraction.description: A large-scale and diverse dataset for robotic failure analysis and correction, comprising 9,440 erroneous manipulation trajectories and 78,623 QA pairs across 16 diverse tasks and 53 scenes in both simulation and real-world environments. The dataset includes six types of failures organized across three hierarchical levels of error (task planning error, motion planning error, and execution control error), with eight question types covering task understanding, failure analysis, and failure correction.
extraction.creator: Weifeng Lu, Minghao Ye, Zewei Ye, Ruihan Tao, Shuo Yang, Bo Zhao; School of AI, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Xiamen University, Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data collected through simulation in ManiSkill environment augmented with YCB Object Dataset and scenes from ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR, and real-world data collected via teleoperation using SO-100 robotic arm. For each custom task, expert policies were defined by specifying target end-effector poses for each substage, with feasible paths and trajectories generated using motion planning. Failure data generated by replacing original expert policy with code snippets that generate erroneous trajectories at selected substages.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Software Collection, Manual Human Curator, Direct measurement
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Simulation data from ManiSkill environment with YCB Object Dataset objects and ReplicaCAD/AI2-THOR scenes. Real-world data collected via teleoperation using SO-100 robotic arm with three synchronized viewpoints (wrist-mounted, top-down, and front-left cameras) along with control signals.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: To generate failure data, the original expert policy was replaced with code snippets that generate erroneous trajectories at selected substages, causing the overall robotic task to fail. Each robotic failure video was recorded along with a corresponding descriptive text including the substage where the failure occurred, the taxonomy of failure, and a detailed textual explanation of the error.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Manual data cleaning was performed to remove trajectories where motion planning failed and did not align with corresponding textual descriptions. Approximately 75% of the collected data was retained after cleaning.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Raw data annotated to construct video-based QA samples corresponding to eight question types. For five question types (task identification, task planning, failure detection, failure identification, and failure locating), reference answers were directly extracted from textual descriptions. For three types (failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction), GPT-4o was utilized with both video and textual description as inputs to generate reference answers. All GPT-4o outputs were manually reviewed and corrected to ensure annotation quality.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All outputs from GPT-4o were manually reviewed and corrected to ensure annotation quality.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4o for generating reference answers for failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction questions
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The current integration of the RoboFAC model into VLA-controlled robotic systems is not yet seamless. The success rate in real-world tasks remains subject to further enhancement, largely due to the VLA model's limited ability to follow complex natural language instructions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluation of multimodal models for robotic failure analysis and correction. The dataset is used for training models capable of task understanding, failure analysis (detection, identification, locating, explanation), and failure correction (high-level and low-level). The model can be integrated into real-world VLA control pipelines as an external critic providing correction instructions.

name.evidence: RoboFAC: A Comprehensive Framework for Robotic Failure Analysis and Correction

description.evidence: we present a Robotic Failure Analysis and Correction (RoboFAC) framework to address this issue. Firstly, we construct RoboFAC dataset comprising 9,440 erroneous manipulation trajectories and 78,623 QA pairs across 16 diverse tasks and 53 scenes in both simulation and real-world environments.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We collect the simuluation data for 14 robotic tasks in the ManiSkill environment [25], augmented with objects from the YCB Object Dataset [26] to increase object diversity and scenes from ReplicaCAD [27] and AI2-THOR [28] to enrich environmental diversity. For each custom task, we first define an expert policy by specifying target end-effector poses for each substage, and the feasible paths and trajectories for the robotic arm to reach these poses are generated using motion planning. To generate failure data, we replace the original expert policy with a code snippet that generates an erroneous trajectory at the selected substage, causing the overall robotic task to fail.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Given the motion planning for the robotic arm occasionally failed, resulting in trajectories that did not align with the corresponding textual descriptions, we manually performed thorough data cleaning and retained approximately 75% of the collected data.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Although we have demonstrated that the RoboFAC model's correction suggestions can effectively assist the VLA model in recovering from failures, our current integration of the model into the VLA-controlled robotic system is not yet seamless... Despite these improvements, the success rate remains subject to further enhancement, largely due to the VLA model's limited ability to follow complex natural language instructions.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: Leveraging our dataset, we develop RoboFAC model, which is capable of Task Understanding, Failure Analysis and Failure Correction...
